newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI up a touch after Gencor nickel deal.
newsitem.headline: QNI up a touch after Gencor nickel deal.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer QNI Ltd rose just slightly in active trade early on Thursday, despite some expectations the nickel merger deal with Gencor announced late on Wednesday would spark a sharp rally.
QNI was up five cents at A$2.73 by 10.15 (0015 GMT) on volume of over 2.6 million shares traded.
Earlier, some brokers said the deal valued QNI shares at A$3.40 to A$3.50 a share and there had been early bids on the Australian Stock Exchange system of A$3.30 a share.
"I'm surprised that they're not trading at a higher level. We think the announcement makes for a stronger company," said Ivan Mitchell, a broker at Brisbane brokerage Nevitts Ltd.
"Our back of the envelope valuation was that they'd be worth something over A$3.00," he said.
Other brokers and analysts said institutional investors digesting the deal overnight had decided the deal appeared more favourable to Gencor than QNI.
"It's quite a favourable deal for the Gencor operation," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"It's earnings per share negative for the stock over the medium term," the analyst said, adding Gencor appeared to have bought into QNI at around A$2.30 to A$2.40 a share.
QNI Ltd announced on Wednesday that it was merging with the nickel arm of Gencor, giving the South African mining house control of the company.

The Queensland-based company said the merger would result in a company with a market value of about A$2.3 billion and allow the two companies to achieve significant cuts to nickel production costs. QNI is currently valued at around A$1.1 billion. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
